# Count the relation generated by partition blocks

*Medium · [Set theory](index.md)*

A set is partitioned into blocks $\{a,b,c\}$, $\{d\}$ and $\{e,f\}$. Define xRy when x,y lie in the same block. How many ordered pairs does R contain?

```answer
{"answer":{"kind":"integer","expected":"14","checker_scope":"Exact declared bounded result, explicit interval description or selected statement only; no unrestricted set proof or new checkpoint objective is automatically certified."}}
```

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Every ordered pair within a block is present, including loops.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Pairs from distinct blocks cannot occur, so the block contributions are disjoint.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Worked solution</summary>

An equivalence relation is the disjoint union of each block Cartesian square.

1. The three-element block contributes $3^2=9$ pairs.
2. The singleton contributes one loop, and the two-element block contributes $2^2=4$ pairs.
3. The total is $9+1+4=14$.

</details>
